title: Cohort-tempo adaptive scheduler for controlled model introductions
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Design and implement an adaptive canary scheduler that introduces model variants to cohorts on a tempo-based (pulsed) schedule rather than purely linear steps. The system will support cohort definitions, pulse/ramp policies, shadow probing, and automated rollback triggers driven by statistical detectors and SLO contracts. Goal: reduce false positives during launches, allow controlled oscillatory exposure for fragile models, and integrate with Console for visibility and manual overrides.
acceptance_criteria: API to define cohort-tempo rollout exists with schema validated in Console
Scheduler can execute pulsed ramps (pulse width, period, growth factor) and fall back to linear/step schedules
Shadow probing can route X% of traffic to variant while keeping production latency SLOs
Automated rollback triggers fire on two independent statistical detectors (regression on latency and top-level correctness metric)
Telemetry surfaces per-cohort breakdowns in Console and Playbook links for failed rollouts
E2E test harness simulates traffic and verifies safe fallback under synthetic capacity drops
tasks: Write RFC with tempo-based schedule model and compare to linear stepper
Define rollout CRD/schema and validation rules
Implement scheduler core: pulse generator, cohort allocator, admission controller
Integrate with existing traffic router and KV cache expiry semantics
Implement statistical detectors: A/B chi-square for correctness, CUSUM for latency regressions
Console UX: per-cohort visualization, manual hold/resume/fallback actions
Automated canary test harness and chaos scenarios (node drain, GPU OOM)
Documentation and runbook including postmortem checklist
comments: 2025-02-18 - Maya Thompson: Initial ticket created. Problem statement: many recent launches produced noisy metrics during steady linear ramps; product teams asked for a safer, oscillatory/pulsed introduction to let caches and KV states stabilize between pulses.

2025-02-20 - Arjun Patel: Proposal to model pulse generation as Poisson-driven bursts with configurable refractory period. Trade-off: Poisson feels more natural for traffic bursts but harder to reason about percentage stability. Action: prototype both fixed-period pulses and Poisson jitter variant.

2025-02-24 - Lina Gomez (PM): PM feedback: must expose simple presets (fast, safe, conservative) for PMs and non-experts. Also require default SLO contracts for latency and error rate at cohort level. Logged design link in Confluence.

2025-02-26 - Dave Chen (SRE): Raised concern about coordinating pulses across multiple regions; suggested TTL-aligned cohort tokens in the routing layer and a centralized pulse leader per-region. Added dependency on ENG-12033 for regional rollout coordination.

2025-03-01 - Arjun Patel: Spike results: pulse ramps reduced transient metric noise by ~18% on internal canary compared to 10-step linear over same duration. Noted higher memory pressure due to repeated KV cache repopulation—added task to evaluate cache warmup strategies.

2025-03-03 - Maya Thompson: Design decision: implement both fixed-period pulse and jittered pulse (Poisson) in scheduler; default preset 'safe-tempo' uses fixed pulses with 5-minute width and 10-minute gap. Added acceptance criteria for two statistical detectors and console override buttons.

2025-03-03 - Security Review: Alice Park: Scoped review not required for initial rollout; audit logging to be included for cohort actions. Marked security_review_required=false but added runbook for audits.
notes: Statistical detectors: require at least 2 independent signals before auto-rollback to reduce blast radius (e.g., latency CUSUM + error-rate increase using sequential probability ratio test)
Default cohort sizes: small (1%), medium (10%), large (25%); allow custom cohort expressions (user segments by region, API key, cookie hash)
Fallback behavior: immediate fallback to previous model variant if rollback triggers hit AND overall cluster capacity unaffected; if capacity impact detected, throttle and notify SRE
Integrate canary decision logs with Console timeline and link to Incident-Playbook templates
